title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across the following domains: API standards, coding standards, infrastructure (IaC) standards, model-serving standards, observability standards, performance objectives, and a canonical ADR pattern. The goal is to provide a single reference for engineers and reviewers to ensure consistent design and operational quality across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Principles:
- Developer-first: APIs and patterns must be simple and predictable for client engineers.
- Production-readiness: Designs must be observable, testable, and support rollbacks.
- Cost-awareness: Architecture choices should reference unit-cost implications (batching, quantization, routing).
- Backwards compatibility: Maintain clear compatibility guarantees and migration paths.
- Security & privacy by design: Default to least privilege, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, and auditability.

1) API Standards
- API surface: All external-facing endpoints (hosted API) and public internal contract services must use OpenAPI 3.1 spec for schema & contracts.
- Versioning: Use major-version path versioning (e.g., /v1/generate). Minor changes must be additive only. Breaking changes require a migration plan or new major version.
- Request/response standard fields (required):
  - request_id (UUID)
  - client_id (string)
  - model (string)
  - model_version (string or semver)
  - input (string/object)
  - parameters (object, optional)
- Error handling: Use structured error objects with fields: code, message, type, retryable (boolean), guidance (string).
- Pagination & streaming: For streaming responses use server-sent events (SSE) or websocket conventions documented in the OpenAPI extensions. For list endpoints use cursor-based pagination.
- Example (OpenAPI fragment):
  {
    "paths": {
      "/v1/generate": {
        "post": {
          "summary": "Text generation",
          "requestBody": {
            "content": {
              "application/json": {
                "schema": {
                  "$ref": "#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest"}
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }

API review checklist (required before merge): owner, contract doc, OpenAPI diff, backwards-compatibility rationale, load test plan, auth config, SLO changes if any.

2) Coding Standards
- Languages: Primary services should use Go (backend infra/runtime), Python (applied ML tooling), and TypeScript (console/frontend).
- Formatting: Enforce gofmt/goimports, black for Python, and Prettier/ESLint for TypeScript.
- Static analysis: CI must run linters (golangci-lint, mypy/ruff, eslint) and disallow new critical/high findings.
- Testing: Require unit tests with >= 80% coverage for service-level code; integration tests for cross-service contracts.
- Dependency policy: Prefer pinned dependencies, require security scan (OSS) and license review for third-party packages.
- Example lint config snippet:
  go: { "linters": ["govet", "staticcheck"] }

3) Infrastructure & IaC Standards
- IaC: All infra must be defined in Terraform modules stored in the terraform/ monorepo. Reuse standard modules for networking, IAM, and monitoring.
- Environments: Maintain separate accounts/projects for dev/staging/prod. No credentials or secrets in VCS.
- Tagging: All cloud resources must include tags: service, owner_team, cost_center, environment.
- Network: Private subnets for sensitive workloads; minimum required inbound rules. VPC peering or Transit Gateway patterns must be documented.
- Secrets & keys: Use KMS/HSM for production key storage. Customer-managed keys required for Private deployments.
- Change management: Significant infra changes require design doc + plan and must be reviewed in the infra standards board.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model packaging: Must include metadata: model_name, model_version, architecture, tokenizer_spec, expected_sequence_lengths, recommended_quantization_profile.
- Model catalog: All served models must be registered in the model catalog with performance profiles (p50/p95 latency, throughput, token cost estimates).
- Versioning & rollouts: Use immutable model artifacts and a rollout plan (canary -> ramp -> full). Each rollout must include evaluation against a regression prompt set.
- Quantization profiles: Maintain quantization recommendations per model and workload; include fallback to full-precision during regressions.
- KV cache & prefix caching: Explicitly define cache keys and TTLs; document KV cache invalidation rules when model or tokenizer changes.
- Safety & filtering: Integrate the quality guardrails pipeline for model outputs; ensure model-level safety metadata is present.
- Example rollout steps:
  1. Prepare model artifact and performance profile in catalog.
  2. Deploy to canary pool (1-5% traffic) with A/B route.
  3. Run automated evals and monitor metrics for 24-72 hours.
  4. If OK, ramp to 25%, then 100% with monitoring and rollback policy.

5) Observability Standards
- Telemetry: Emit structured logs (JSON), metrics (Prometheus), and distributed traces (OTel).
- Required metrics: request_count, request_error_count (label by error_type), latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), tokens_generated, model_cache_hit_rate.
- SLOs & alerts: SLOs must be defined at route and model level. Default SLOs (hosted): availability 99.9% monthly, p95 latency <= 500ms for short-generation (<128 tokens) routes.
- Alerting: Use burn-rate alerting for SLOs, and threshold alerts for error spikes and model degradation. Pager escalation is defined in eng-sre runbooks.
- Logs: Retain logs for 90 days for standard tier; configure longer retention for dedicated/enterprise per contract. Ensure PII/redaction rules are enforced at ingestion.

6) Performance Standards
- Benchmarks: All serving configurations must include benchmark artifacts: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput at target concurrency, GPU memory utilization, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Target SLO examples (default hosted):
  - p50 latency (<=128 tokens): <= 120ms
  - p95 latency (<=128 tokens): <= 500ms
  - throughput (batching efficiency): target >= 70% of theoretical throughput at steady-state
  - cold-start: < 2s for warm pool-enabled deployments; < 10s for cold instances
- Load testing: Before increasing traffic on a new model or configuration, run synthetic load tests that simulate request distributions (seq length, parameters, concurrency).
- Performance regression policy: Any regression >10% p95 latency or >15% cost/unit must trigger rollback and a regression triage.

7) ADR (Architecture Decision Record) Pattern
- Location: Store ADRs in the confluence architecture directory and mirror in repo under docs/adrs/.
- Required ADR fields: id, title, status, context, decision, consequences, date, owners, related_pages.
- ADR template (example):
  - id: ADR-2026-02
  - title: Standardize model version pinning across runtime
  - status: accepted
  - context: We need reproducible inference results across deployments and safety for rollbacks.
  - decision: All runtime requests must include model_version; default behavior will treat unspecified versions as "latest-stable" with documented semantics.
  - consequences: Better reproducibility, extra catalog bookkeeping, small UX cost for clients.
  - owners: eng-serving-runtime

8) Rollout & Change Management Checklist
- For any change that affects API contracts, observability, infra, or model-serving behavior include:
  1. RFC/Design doc + ADR (if decision-level).
  2. OpenAPI/spec diff and migration plan.
  3. Load and regression test plan.
  4. Rollout steps + canary config + automatic rollback triggers.
  5. Updated runbooks + runbook smoke tests.
  6. Communication plan (release notes, slack channel, on-call notification).

9) Ownership and Review Cadence
- Standards owner: eng-platform owns maintenance of this consolidated standards doc.
- Review cadence: Quarterly review cycle; ad-hoc reviews for urgent infra/security changes.
- Approval: Significant changes require cross-team review (eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, security-and-compliance, product).

10) Related Resources
- Links (internal):
  - eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture (architecture deep-dive)
  - eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (SLO policy)
  - applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding (model onboarding checklist)
  - engineering-templates/openapi-guidelines (OpenAPI guidance)

Appendix: Example ADR (full)
- id: ADR-2026-07
- title: Select default quantization profile for LLM v2 family
- status: accepted
- date: 2026-02-10
- context: Multiple quantization options exist with tradeoffs between latency and quality.
- decision: Default to q4_0 for balanced cost/latency for inference on GPU-backed dedicated pools. Profiles per workload will be documented in the model catalog and enforced in deployment configs.
- consequences: Reduced token cost for most production workloads; maintain a documented fallback to fp16 for high-quality-sensitive workloads.
- owners: research/applied-ml, eng-serving-runtime

If you have questions or encounter gaps, open a PR against this page or contact the standards owners in #eng-architecture.
